Explore Fall Color in Columbus This Autumn

Are you enjoying seeing the leaves starting to change? Columbus should see peak fall color over the next several weeks! This is your chance to get outside to exercise in the cooler weather while also enjoying the stunning color of the leaves around Columbus. There is nothing better than walking outside on a fall day and seeing the colorful red, orange and yellow leaves changing the look of your favorite park. Instead of seeing other people’s fall photos online, take some time to explore some new parks, and find some gorgeous fall color on your own! Goodale and Schiller parks are expected to have the highest potential for diverse fall color this year. Did you know that you have more than 400 Columbus parks in which to explore Ohio fall color? Explore a new park today!

FiftyPlus Basketball Registration Closes Soon

Slam-dunk this fall season, and join the 50+ basketball league. Both individuals and teams are welcome. Need to brush up on your skills? Not to worry, open basketball times are available at Barack Community Center to help you prepare for the season. Check out open basketball dates. Save the date, registration will open on Oct. 15. This 10-week season begins Nov. 5. Learn more about league pricings and how to register.

Bring the Family to Watch "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow"

Come out and watch young actors bring in the Halloween season during the production of “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow.” The whole family will have a hauntingly good time watching the Columbus Performing Arts Players youth tell the spooky tale of Ichabod Crane and his encounter with the Headless Horseman. The performances will be held at the Columbus Performing Arts Center's Van Fleet Theatre Oct. 20-21 at 7:30 p.m. and Oct. 22 at 2 p.m. Tickets are free! Learn more about the upcoming performances.

Give Back to Your Community During Adopt a Center This Holiday Season

Although the holidays may seem like a long way off, consider giving back to those in need. Through the community centers, Adopt a Center provides toys and food to families in need during the holiday season. The goal is to relieve some of the financial burden many families experience during the holidays. Make sure every child in your community is able to experience the magic of receiving a gift during the holiday season! Find out more and how to donate.

item.title: A Message from Director Reese: Congratulations on CAPRA Accreditation!
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Dear CRPD Team,

All I can say is--THANK YOU! 

I am so excited that we officially were named as a CAPRA-accredited agency at the NRPA conference in Dallas last night! 

For years, I've wanted our department to earn CAPRA accreditation. I know we are one of the best agencies in the nation, and we have some of the best staff. And it's time the entire industry knows it.

Today, they do! We are now recognized as part of the top 6 percent of all recreation and parks agencies!

This is everyone's honor. Each day, you come in and focus on serving our residents. You deliver programming, services and facilities that help residents connect with nature, focus on their wellness and explore creative pursuits - and connect with each other. Your work makes our community a better place, and it's why we earned this honor. 

I also want to thank the team that pulled together all of the information necessary to submit our application. That took hours and hours of time and a lot of dedication, and you did it while staying on top of the rest of your work. A special thanks to Craig Murphy, who led this effort.

Again, congratulations, and thank you for all that you do! I look forward to celebrating with everyone in a few weeks at the All Staff Meeting on Nov. 1--it will be day full of fun! 

~Bernita   

Bernita A. Reese, M.S., CPRP
Director, Columbus Recreation and Parks Department

item.description:

Park Spotlight: Big Walnut Park

Have you visited Big Walnut Park? Located at 5000 E. Livingston Ave., this 136-acre community park is in the Mid-East community, near Reynoldsburg. This park has many amenities, including one of five city dog parks, a pond, a playground, recently renovated tennis courts, ball diamonds, basketball courts and Far East Community Center, which is located at 1826 Lattimer Dr. It also has a .8-mile paved path, the Big Walnut Park Shelterhouse, access to the Big Walnut Creek and the Big Walnut Trail. Consider exploring Big Walnut Park today!

Friday Night Frights Softball Tournament Registration Opens Tomorrow

Enjoy the scariest night of softball in town! Friday Night Frights, the yearly Halloween-season adult softball tournament, is always lots of fun and is hosted at Lou Berliner Sports Park, located at 1300 Deckenbach Road. Registration opens tomorrow so be sure to sign up. Find more information on softball pricings, leagues and tournaments.

See the New Exhibits at the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center

Check out the two new exhibits at the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center! “Art from the Day of the Dead Festival,” hosted in the Loft Gallery, presents a collective exhibition of local artists inspired by the Day of the Dead, a Hispanic celebration of life, death and everything in between. A reception takes place on Tuesday, Oct. 11, from 6-7:30 p.m.

Meanwhile, “The Sky’s the Limit: Quilt Transformation,” hosted in the Main Gallery, expands the definition of what quilting is by incorporating multiple media, as well as moving out from the wall with three-dimensional pieces. A reception takes place on Friday, Oct. 13, from 6-8 p.m.

Learn more about these and other upcoming art exhibits.

Share Your Feedback on the New Pickleball Courts at Mock Park

Calling all pickleballers! If you enjoy pickleball, you are invited to attend the open house for Mock Park on Wednesday, Oct. 18, from 5-7 p.m. at the Willis Athletic Complex, located at 2520 Mock Road, Columbus. Mock Park will be welcoming new pickleball courts. Your input is needed to determine the desired functionality, design and amenities of these new pickleball courts. You can stop by the open house to share your feedback anytime between 5-7 p.m. Snacks will be provided.

Plant a Free Tree in Your Yard This Fall

Did you know that fall is a great time to plant a tree in your yard? Planting trees on private property is crucial to increasing Columbus’ canopy cover to 40 percent by 2050!​ Get tips on planting a tree, and get a free tree from Green Columbus on Oct. 21 at the Linden nursery. Register for your free tree today!

Youth Basketball Registration for Fall II

Does your student like to shoot hoops at home? If so, sign them up for a basketball team. Registration for youth basketball opens on Tuesday, Oct. 3, so be sure to save the date on your calendars! This is a great way to get your child engaged and active with other kids in their community. Check out more information on pricings, dates and times.

Volunteer at the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center

Are you looking for ways to contribute to the arts community? The Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center has a variety of volunteer opportunities for you to choose from! Volunteers work hand-in-hand with the Friends of the Cultural Arts Center to help provide support services that help meet the center's goals and mission, organize programs and events, perform routine tasks and much more. Learn how you can become a volunteer today.

Help Beautify Your Local Community Center

Do you have a green thumb? Then join friends and neighbors in planting a new landscape design at your local community center! You can participate in planting at four different sites between Oct. 4-21:

  • Adams Community Center: Oct. 4, 9 a.m.-12 p.m.

item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Learn About Your Neighborhood’s Street Trees

Did you know that Columbus has more than 125,000 street trees? Over the last three years, the location, species and condition of each tree was collected and documented. While inventorying the trees, information about where new street trees could be planted was collected for the first time, and there are 96,000 sites available. Having all of this information in one place will help protect and grow a healthy urban forest.

Reports for all 41 Columbus neighborhoods are now available so you can learn more about the trees in your community. Check out the citywide summary report, as well as the report for your neighborhood!

These efforts are part of the Urban Forestry Master Plan. Read more about what's been accomplished recently! 

Get Active at Home

Are you someone who has limited time or who prefers to exercise by yourself? If this sounds like you, then make sure you visit the Get Active at Home web series. This free web series explores a range of workouts you can do at home, including Tai Chi, HIIT, chair yoga and other exercises. Look for your favorite class or instructor, or try something new! Follow along with these free workout videos from the comfort of your own home today. 

Become a Star During the "Inspecting Carol" Open Auditions

You can get a chance to be on stage during the upcoming performance of "Inspecting Carol" with the Columbus Performing Arts Players during their open auditions! This comedic play is about a company that is looking to change up their usual Christmas tradition of performing “A Christmas Carol.” The Columbus Performing Arts Players will perform the show Dec. 7-9.

If you're an aspiring thespian who is age 18 or older, try out during open auditions Oct. 3 and 4 at 6:30 p.m. at the Columbus Performing Arts Center, located at 549 Franklin Ave. Learn more about the upcoming auditions and performances.

Come Out to the Open House for Kilbourne Run Sports Park

Have you heard about the Kilbourne Run Sports Park project? If you haven’t and would like to learn more – or if you have and would like to provide input - come out to the open house hosted at Woodward Park Community Center, located 5147 Karl Road, on Wednesday, Oct. 4. The open house runs from 6-7:30 p.m., and anyone can drop in during that window, as well as ask questions and provide feedback on the current design. Kilbourne Run Sports Park is part of the Community Sports Park project, which makes significant investments in sports facilities across the City. Make sure you add the open house date to your calendar!

Join Us for Pollinator Field Day Next Month

Are you interested in learning about pollinators, and protecting their habitat? Pollinators are animals that help carry pollen from plant to plant, such as butterflies, bees and birds! Pollinator Field Day will be held on Saturday, Oct. 7, from 10 a.m.-1 p.m. at the prairie at Whetstone Park. You can volunteer, you will remove invasive species and help maintain the pollinator spaces at the prairie. This family-friendly event will also offer free programming for families where you can learn more about pollinators. Register for your spot to volunteer today; registration is NOT required to join in the educational activities. 

Adult Volleyball Registration Closing Soon

If you’re still interested in registering for an adult volleyball league, don’t wait too long! Registration is set to close on Sept. 22 so make sure you sign up now if you’re interested in showing off your spiking and setting skills. Volleyball is a great way to stay fit and stay active. Learn more about league offerings, game times and pricing.

Make Your Own Sidewalk Chalk at Home

Take advantage of the last warm days of the summer season by enjoying art outside! Join Miss Suzanne, a Columbus Recreation and Parks instructor, on the department's YouTube channel for her Art With Kids @ Home series. She has an instructional video to teach you and your family how you can make your own sidewalk chalk at home. With just three simple household ingredients, you can begin making beautiful art all around the neighborhood. Check out how you can paint your sidewalks with your homemade chalk designs today!

Join Teen Outdoor Day, Presented by Girls Empowerment Day

Do you know teen girls who are looking for fun activities to do outdoors this fall? Then consider Teen Outdoor Day, presented by Columbus Recreation and Parks Girls Empowerment! This event will be held at McKnight Outdoor Education Center, located at 3228 Indian Village Road on Saturday, Sept 23. Teen Outdoor Day is a safe and free fun-filled day for girls ages 12-18 featuring great activities such as canoeing, archery, birding and fire building. This event runs from 10 a.m.-3 p.m. Space is limited so make sure you register today via ACTIVEnet!

item.title: Thanks for a Great Summer, Ohio Blueway Trails, Adult Basketball Leagues, Conversation and Coffee and Rise Up CBUS!
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Thanks for a Great Summer, Columbus!

There is something special about summer here in Columbus! Your involvement in the department’s programs, classes, camps and events made it a fantastic summer. Here are a few highlights from the summer:

  • 241,000 summer meals served
  • 9,400 kids attended summer camps and programs
  • 47,000 residents cooled off in pools
  • 223,000 people attended 37 community events and festivals
  • 200,000 youth and adults participated in sports leagues
  • 64,000 people celebrated 1,081 events at our indoor and outdoor rental facilities
  • 1,800 volunteers served 4,500 hours in the outdoor season
  • 250 teens and young adults gained work experience and jobs skills through the APPS Job Readiness Program
  • 101,000 rounds of golf were played
  • 3,200 people participated in classes and programs through the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center

Thank you for participating in summer programming! Fall session 1 activities and classes are now open so register today. Learn more about what is available at Columbus Recreation and Parks Department.

Paddle Along the Central Ohio Blueway Trails

Have you checked out the Central Ohio Blueway Trails? If you enjoy kayaking or canoeing, the weather is still warm enough to check them out! The 8.94-mile state-designated Olentangy Water Trail runs from the Broad Meadows pedestrian bridge downtown to the confluence of the Scioto River. There are four boating hazards (lowhead dams) along the trail, so make sure you use the designated portage locations to walk your kayak or canoe around those obstacles so you stay safe. Learn about the hazards and the points of interest along this water trail.

There are also paddlesports lockers available to rent near Lower.com Field, at the Lower Olentangy Park and boat launch if you want to keep your kayak or canoe near downtown. Learn more about the Central Ohio Blueway Trails.

Adult Basketball League Registration Opens Tomorrow

Begin this fall season with a slam dunk by joining an adult basketball league! Registration opens tomorrow, Friday, Sept. 8, at 10 a.m. The eight-week season begins Wednesday, Oct. 4, and features weekly games so you can have fun with your friends and stay in shape. Learn about dates, times, pricing and more.

Enjoy Coffee and Artist Talks During Conversations and Coffee

Conversations and Coffee is the city's longest-running series of artist talks. On select Thursdays, you can enjoy your lunch break from 12-1 p.m. at the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center with other art enthusiasts and artists from different corners of the world. This month's free artist talks are:

  • Sept. 14: Linda Turvy, curator of the Many Muses exhibition in the Loft Gallery
  • Sept. 21: Voszi Douglas, a fashion designer
  • Sept. 28: Tim and Ted Murphy, creators of the Strange and Known Things exhibition in the Main Gallery 

Bring your lunch, enjoy freshly brewed coffee and hear about the inspiration of local and global artists during Conversations and Coffee!

Only a Few More Chances to Enjoy Free Food, Music and Resources at Rise Up CBUS!

There are only two more opportunities to enjoy all of the fun Rise Up CBUS has to offer! Bring the whole family on Sept. 14 from 4:30 to 7:30 p.m. at Eastpointe Christian Church, 745 Waggoner Road in Blacklick. Find out more about this event and its collaboration with the Columbus Department of Neighborhoods.

Dear CRPD Team,

Every year from Sept. 15-Oct. 15, the United States recognizes Hispanic Heritage Month to celebrate the histories, cultures and contributions of generations of Hispanic Americans  who have helped to shape this diverse country. 

This year, the Latino Heritage Month Committee is hosting the Latino Heritage Parade on Saturday, Sept. 16, to kick off this year's celebrations. The inaugural committee was formed out of the office of Columbus City Councilmember Lourdes Barroso de Padilla to promote visibility, cultural awareness and togetherness during Latino Heritage month in hopes of creating lasting impact in the greater Columbus community.

Join your coworkers and celebrate culture, community and diversity as we parade through downtown Columbus. Register by Tuesday, Sept. 12 at 5 p.m. by clicking on the button below.

Help Remove Invasive Species This Weekend

Are you trying to find a way to give back to your local community? Consider volunteering at the upcoming Community Conservation Day on Saturday, Sept. 2! You can volunteer to do invasive species removal at Madison Mills Park, located at 3257 Williams Road. Removing invasive species is crucial conservation efforts right here in Columbus, and Columbus Recreation and Parks will provide direction and equipment to make this a great experience. This event will be held from 9 a.m.-12 p.m., and it is a fun option for individuals or groups. Register for your spot online.

Senior Wellness Jamboree Registration Opens Sept. 5

Don't miss out on registration for the Senior Wellness Jamboree! Registration opens on Tuesday, Sept. 5, for this fun-filled event slated for Friday, Oct. 6. The Senior Wellness Jamboree will take place at the Franklin Park Adventure Center from 9 a.m.-2 p.m. Participants will take a stroll through the park together, as well as learn about tips and resources for maintaining a healthy lifestyle, participate in classes and activities, and win prizes. Lunch will be provided to those who register before Monday, Sept. 25. Learn more about this yearly event, and register.

Start a New Hobby This Fall

You can get involved in fun and affordable art classes for beginner and experienced artists at the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center! Registration begins Saturday, Sept. 2, at 8:30 a.m. Explore creative classes like painting, jewelry, sculpting, drawing, printmaking, pottery and much more. Class session 5 begins Monday, Sept. 11, and will include seven to eight weeks of sessions where you will receive in-depth, hands-on experience. Learn more about all the classes offered and how to register.

Attend the Last Edition of Wednesdays on the Green of 2023

Have you attended Wednesdays on the Green yet? If the answer is no, swing by Dorrian Green, which is the park located on the lawn in front of COSI, on Sept. 6 from 5-8 p.m. for the last edition of Wednesdays on the Green this year. Bring lawn chairs or a blanket and enjoy listening to local band The Floorwalkers for a concert you won't want to miss! Snacks and non-alcoholic beverages will be available to purchase from COSI on the plaza. This event is presented in partnership with Columbus Downtown Development Corporation. Learn more about this free event.

item.title: Public Tree Code, Adult Kickball, Loft Gallery Exhibition and City Leaders Academy
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Help Increase Protections for Columbus' Trees

Did you know Columbus is strengthening its protections for public trees? Public trees grow on City-owned property, like street trees and park trees. The City is updating its public tree code, which spells out specific protections for these important trees. These protections will help better preserve and grow Columbus' tree canopy.

You can help shape these regulations, as well as the City's first Tree Technical Manual. Share your thoughts now through Sept. 22.

Adult Kickball League Registration is Currently Open

If you were the champ at playing kickball as a kid, imagine showing off your skills now! Registration for adult kickball leagues is currently open, but sign up before it closes on Sept. 1. This four-week season begins the week of Sept. 12, and games are played at Lou Berliner Sports Park. Find out more information on league pricing, game times and more.

A New Loft Gallery Exhibition is Coming Soon

The Loft Gallery within the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center is a smaller intimate exhibition area for up-and-coming artists. The latest exhibition to come to the Loft Gallery is “Many Muses.” Curated by Linda Turvy, it focuses on her efforts to have a minimal impact to the environment in her arts as she often utilizes repurposed paints, found objects and other recycled goods. Many of the pieces are characterized as bricolage, derived from a French word meaning a construction or creation from a diverse range of available and often unconventional things.

Be the first to see the exhibit at the open reception for the "Many Muses" exhibition on Friday, Aug. 25, from 6-8 p.m. Come out and enjoy this free event where you can enjoy complimentary food and drinks, and view unique pieces of art.

Application Deadline for City Leaders Academy Extended to Sept. 8

Do you have a sixth through nineth grader who is interested in helping lead Columbus into the future? Encourage them to apply for the City Leaders Academy! During this nine-month program, they will learn about the inner workings of the City of Columbus, increase their citizenship skills and receive mentoring from City and community leaders, preparing them to become a community leader.

The deadline for applications has been extended to Friday, Sept. 8, at 5 p.m. Applications may be scanned and emailed to ANCombs@columbus.gov or returned by hard copy to the Jerry Hammond Center, located at 1111 E. Broad St., 43205. Hard copies may be mailed or left with the guard desk. Learn more, and start filling out your application now!

item.title: Trails Updates, Nite Owl Classic Registration, Main Gallery Art Exhibition and Outdoor Pools Season Closing
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

New Franklinton/Souder Avenue Trail Connector on the Scioto Trail

If you use the Scioto Trail, don’t miss this information about the Franklinton/Souder Avenue trail connector, which will build a new pedestrian bridge over the Scioto River and a new trail along Souder Avenue to West Broad Street. The project will tie in thousands of residents and employees to the regional trail network and complete the popular 3-mile downtown trail loop, which includes the Scioto Mile, COSI and the National Veterans Memorial and Museum. The trail will undergo construction to build the new pedestrian bridge and trail, complete with lighting and additional tree plantings.

For everyone’s safety, the trail is temporarily closed at Souder Avenue. A temporary detour path has been constructed on the north side of the Scioto River, which will allow the path to remain open heading upstream to 5th Avenue. See the detour map. Construction is set to be completed in July 2024. Check out the department’s facility and alerts updates page to find information on alerts, closures and hazards for the department’s trails, parks and facilities. 

Nite Owl Classic Softball Registration Opens Tomorrow

Pull a fun all-nighter and join the Nite Owl Classic Softball Tournament at Lou Berliner Sports Park. This session offers both men’s and women’s divisions. Registration is available starting tomorrow, Aug. 18, through Sept. 1. Check out the schedules, pricing, and more! 

Get Transported into the World of Art at the Cultural Arts Center

You and your family can enjoy viewing beautiful works of art from local to international artists at the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center. The next main gallery exhibition will include art from brothers Ted and Tim Murphy. They will bring a visual treat that combines exquisite watercolor and gouache scenes from nature with mixed-media figurative commentaries on the human condition. The exhibition's opening reception is Friday, Aug. 25, from 6-8 p.m. Learn more about this and other upcoming main gallery art exhibitions.

Pool Season is Coming to a Close

As summer begins to wind down, please note that the following pools will close for the season on Sunday, Aug. 20: Lincoln, Marion Franklin, Maryland and Windsor. Meanwhile, the following pools will be open on weekends only beginning Sunday, Aug. 20: Tuttle, Driving Park, Dodge and Glenwood. These four pools will close for the season on Sunday, Sept. 3.

Although the outdoor pools may be done for the year, you can still swim indoors by visiting the Columbus Aquatics Center, located at 1160 Hunter Ave., 43201. The center reopens on Tuesday, Sept. 5. Learn more about the Aquatics Center's offerings.

item.title: Explore Central Ohio Trails, Rent a Sports Field, CBUS Soul Fest and COAAA
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Explore Central Ohio Trails This Month

Summer is one of the best times of the year to check out trails near you! Did you know that central Ohio has more than 230 miles of regional trails? Walking, running, biking and kayaking are great forms of exercise. Learn more about the Central Ohio Greenways trails, which include popular trails like the Olentangy Trail and the Alum Creek Trail. If you are interested in kayaking or canoeing, you can also visit the Central Ohio Blueway Trails, which is the Olentangy River Water Trail. While you're at it, check out some parks with paved paths if you need new places to walk. It’s always a good time to be active so explore some new trails today!

Rent a Cricket Field Today

Did you know that there are three cricket fields available in your local area? You can rent a field at Anheuser-Busch Sports Park, Lazelle Woods and Tuttle Park for just $20 per hour. Find out more information on how to rent fields for various sports.

Jam Out at CBUS Soul Fest

Celebrate Columbus’ vibrant Black culture, music and soul during CBUS Soul Fest, presented by Columbus Recreation and Parks in partnership with Experience Columbus. This one-day event features live music and great food! The concert lineup includes multi-Grammy winner PJ Morton, Avery*Sunshine, The Deal Breakers, MojoFlo and Harmonic Soul.

This free event will take place on Saturday, Aug. 19, from 4-11 p.m. at Genoa Park, located at 303 W. Broad St. Make sure you’re there to take in the experience. Learn more about the event's vendors, stage schedule and more! 

Take Advantage of COAAA’s Services

The Central Ohio Area Agency on Aging (COAAA) plans, funds and delivers services that help older adults and individuals with disabilities remain safe and independent in their homes. With the assistance of area providers, COAAA arranges and coordinates services to help individuals with activities of daily living such as homemaking, transportation, home delivered meals, personal care and more.

COAAA, which is part of Columbus Recreation and Parks, offers education and resources, and advocates for programs and policies that benefit older adults and individuals with disabilities. Notably, the agency manages services for 15,000 people and funds services for another 25,000 older adults. Learn more about all that COAA has to offer.

item.title: National Golf Month, Walk With A Doc, Theatre Auditions, Cap City Experiences and Rise Up CBUS!
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Get Active Outside During National Golf Month

Did you know August is National Golf Month? To celebrate, enjoy one of the six golf courses Columbus Recreation and Parks has in central Ohio! Golfing is a great way to be active and enjoy spending time outside in nature with family or friends. The 18-hole courses are Airport, Champions, Mentel Memorial, Raymond Memorial and Turnberry golf courses. The nine-hole course, Wilson Road Golf Course, located adjacent to Raymond Memorial Golf Course, is ideal for beginning golfers. Don’t let the summer get away from you - book your tee time today at CRPDGolf.com.

Prioritize Your Health with Walk With a Doc

Learn about health and fitness while on a Walk with a Doc! This event is a FiftyPlus program where you can ask questions to certified doctors, participate in fun group activities and earn prizes. If you cannot walk for long, don’t worry, participants of all fitness levels may join and walk at their own pace and distance. Prioritize your health, and don’t miss out on this free event! Check available dates at your local community center.

Let Your Youth Star in the Next Theatre Production at the Columbus Performing Arts Center

The Columbus Performing Arts Players are hosting open audition for their next production, "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow." Washington Irving’s spooktacular classic takes place in the large farming community of Sleepy Hollow in 1790. The townsfolk recount stories of supernatural sightings and unusual occurrences happening in the town, like tales of the Headless Horseman. Get a chance to be in the spotlight by coming to one day of auditions for ages 10-17 on Aug. 5 or 6 at 2 p.m. at the Columbus Performing Arts Center. The performance will be held Oct. 20-22. For more information, contact Geoffrey Martin at GAMartin@columbus.gov or visit the Columbus Performing Arts Center website. 

Two For One: Don't Miss Cap City Experience and Rise Up CBUS! This Saturday

Saturday’s Cap City Experience and Rise Up CBUS! event is not one to miss! This free event for the Marion Franklin community will include food and live music, along with lots of community resources for residents to explore. Make sure you’re there on Saturday, Aug. 5, from 4-8 p.m. at Marion Franklin Community Center, located at 2801 Lockbourne Road, Columbus, 43207.

Marion Franklin pool will be open with free admission from 5-8 p.m. Stop by the check-in tent at the festival for a wristband to get into the pool. This event is done in collaboration with the Columbus Department of Neighborhoods and is sure to be a good time! Learn more information about Cap City Experience and Rise Up CBUS!.
